clue.text: Anger in pub leading to sustained assault

indicators.note: says the pub word comes first and runs on into the anger word

parts.note: a bar is a pub, or the counter in one
rage is fierce anger

explanation.surface: A drinker's fury in the pub ends in a prolonged attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrage is a heavy, continuous bombardment, so a sustained assault in military terms.

clue.text: Benefit everyone received that's subject to inflation

indicators.note: the benefit takes in what follows

parts.note: a boon is a benefit
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A welfare benefit that everyone gets is one that rises with prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inflation' suggests economics, but the definition means a thing that is blown up.
explanation.definitionFit: A balloon is something you inflate, so a fitting subject for being blown up.

clue.text: Old poems of dogma, essentially varied in interpretation

indicators.note: the letters are interpreted freely, so rearranged
essentially points to the essence, the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: Ancient verses expressing dogma are read in different ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' takes G, the middle of 'dogma'; 'in interpretation' rearranges G with VARIED.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rig Veda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, ancient Hindu sacred verse.

clue.text: A long letter

parts.note: to long for is to itch for

explanation.surface: A lengthy piece of correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like a description of the letter, but it is the verb, to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of the letter H as it is spelt out.

clue.text: Lecturer always welcomes a kiss and some money

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in what follows

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always
X represents a kiss
a pound is a sum of money

explanation.surface: A teacher always gets a kiss and some cash.
explanation.definitionFit: One who expounds explains a subject at length, as a lecturer does.

clue.text: Essential couple of coins, one not English

indicators.note: says one of the pair of coins loses a letter, the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: two coins side by side: the cent, and the real of Spain and Brazil

explanation.surface: Two coins are vital, provided one of them isn't English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple of coins' supplies two coin names; 'one not English' takes the E out of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Something central is at the heart of a matter, i.e. essential to it.

clue.text: Employing spades, manage wood

indicators.note: employing means taking on, so the word holds the spades

parts.note: to cope is to manage
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: Woodland managed with spades.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small wood or thicket of trees.

clue.text: Severe pain sends tormented Algerian round the bend

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the bend
tormented means twisted, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a U-bend is a bend shaped like the letter U

explanation.surface: Agony drives a tortured Algerian mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round the bend' means mad in the surface; here the bend is U, which the anagram of ALGERIAN goes round.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuralgia is intense pain along a nerve.

clue.text: Barman almost got up — wrong one!

definitions.note: a crossword joke: a man of musical bars, i.e. a composer

indicators.note: almost drops the final letter

parts.note: rose means got up
a sin is a wrong
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The barman nearly got up, but it was the wrong man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barman' is a composer, someone who writes in bars, and fittingly this one wrote The Barber of Seville.
explanation.definitionFit: Rossini was the Italian composer; composers write music measured in bars.

clue.text: Securing army officer to rise against one he swore to serve?

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel
an army officer swears allegiance to the monarch, the king

explanation.surface: An officer rebelling against the monarch he pledged to serve.
explanation.definitionFit: Locking is fastening or making fast, so securing.

clue.text: Have a fag to improve one's mood

definitions.meaning: fag is British slang for a cigarette, so this means start smoking one
to brighten up or become cheerful

explanation.surface: A smoker reaches for a cigarette to cheer up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fag' is everyday British slang for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both igniting a cigarette and a face brightening with happiness.

clue.text: Deadly acid of copper to engulf huge area shortly

definitions.note: an adjective naming the acid: the answer is the word used before 'acid' in its name

indicators.note: the police officer surrounds what follows

parts.note: copper is slang for a police officer, a PC (police constable)

indicators.note: shortly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Russia is the largest country by area

explanation.surface: A deadly acid made from copper swallows up a vast tract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like the chemical element, apt beside 'acid', but it is the policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Prussic acid is hydrogen cyanide, a notoriously lethal poison, so the word names that deadly acid.

clue.text: All welcome here, but we have not decided on kind of dance music

parts.note: an undecided matter is still open
house is a style of electronic dance music

explanation.surface: Everyone's welcome, though nobody has settled what dance music to play.
explanation.definitionFit: An open house is an event or home where any visitor is welcome.

clue.text: Defence of road going to close, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken, giving something sounding like them

parts.note: a road is an alley, and close means by (nearby): alley by

explanation.surface: A legal defence based on a road that is about to be shut.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'alley by' sounds like the answer, with the first I pronounced long; 'going to' just joins the two parts. Some solvers objected that an alley is hardly a road.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a defence that the accused was elsewhere when the crime happened.

clue.text: Homes in Geordieland are mostly small

parts.note: Geordies come from Tyneside, in the North East of England, NE

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Houses in Newcastle tend to be on the small side.
explanation.walkthrough: Geordies are people from Newcastle and Tyneside in North East England. 'Mostly' cuts ARE to AR.
explanation.definitionFit: To home in on something is to close on it, which is what something that approaches does.

clue.text: Old beast gets up and over, painful to listen to

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: says the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: painful means sore

explanation.surface: An old animal gets up and moves over, groaning in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: SAUR is how 'sore' sounds in a non-rhotic British accent.
explanation.definitionFit: The stegosaur was a plated dinosaur, a beast from prehistoric times.

clue.text: Finding fault with moving divan back and embracing while husband's away

indicators.note: moving with back says the bed is shifted round so it reads the other way
back, with moving, says the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a divan is a kind of bed

indicators.note: while, with away, says something is missing during the embrace: the husband's letter leaves
away says the husband is absent, so his letter leaves the embracing word

parts.note: hugging means embracing
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A spouse criticises the shifting of the divan and cuddles while her husband is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving ... back' turns BED into DEB; 'away' drops H from HUGGING to leave UGGING.
explanation.definitionFit: Debugging is tracking down and removing faults, especially in computer programs.

clue.text: With Indian food, case for ordering cold water

parts.note: a balti is a curry cooked and served in a metal pan

indicators.note: the letters are there to be put in a different order

explanation.surface: Ordering a curry, plus a case of cold water to go with it.
explanation.walkthrough: Balti is a curry style popular in Birmingham, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltic Sea is a chilly northern European sea, so a body of cold water.

clue.text: Popular bet: Reverend to retreat, lacking a lot of backbone

indicators.note: to retreat says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue words lose most of their letters, leaving only a run from within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A popular wager on a vicar's withdrawal suggests he's spineless.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft made 'lacking a lot of backbone' the definition, but 'lacking a lot' is what signals the concealed run (most letters dropped), leaving 'of backbone' as the adjective's definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertebral means relating to the vertebrae, the bones of the spine.

clue.text: Nasty housing relative makes available to view

indicators.note: housing means giving a home to, so the nasty word takes the relative in

parts.note: vile means nasty
a sib, sibling, is a relative

explanation.surface: A nasty piece of work puts up a relative and opens his home to viewers.
explanation.definitionFit: Visible means able to be seen, open to view.

clue.text: Way for Pom to get some seafood?

parts.note: the instruction roll applied to mop turns it over, so it reads as Pom, the Australian name for an English person

explanation.surface: A route by which an Englishman can get some fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pom' is Australian slang for an English person. The answer, read as an instruction, says how to turn MOP into POM: roll it over.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollmop is a pickled herring fillet rolled round a filling, a kind of seafood.

clue.text: Jelly-like film?

parts.note: as can mean like, in the way that
a pic is an informal word for a film or picture

explanation.surface: Is this film a wobbly one?
explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it suggests a film that resembles jelly, but it splits into a definition and two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from meat or fish stock.

clue.text: French city spread over dead flat area

indicators.note: the city is spread round the word that follows

parts.note: Pau is a city in south-west France
late means dead, as in the late king

explanation.surface: A French city sprawls across a dead-flat region.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is a raised area of level ground, a flat tableland.

clue.text: In summary, little bird heading off for stream

indicators.note: puts the bird inside the curt word

parts.note: curt and summary both mean brief and abrupt

indicators.note: the first letter is taken off

parts.note: the wren is a tiny bird

explanation.surface: In a nutshell, a small bird flew off over the brook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In summary' reads as a phrase meaning 'briefly', but 'In' is the insertion signal and 'summary' the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A current is a flow of water, a stream.

clue.text: Nearly half the smelling salts used in coordinated shots

indicators.note: nearly half means fewer than half the letters are kept, here five of eleven

parts.note: sal volatile is the old name for smelling salts

explanation.surface: Smelling salts get used during a volley of gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: Sal volatile is ammonium carbonate used as smelling salts; keeping its first five letters gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, a burst of coordinated shots.

clue.text: Be reasonable — blonde is not that good

parts.note: fair hair is blonde
is shortened to 's
fair means middling, not especially good

explanation.surface: A plea for reason: being blonde isn't such an advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an appeal for just and reasonable treatment, used to tell someone to be fair.

clue.text: Time to put in charges for parish events

indicators.note: says the time letter goes inside

parts.note: fees are charges

explanation.surface: It's time to charge admission to the church events.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetes are outdoor fairs, a common fund-raising event for a parish church.

clue.text: Neckwear almost strangles one philosopher

indicators.note: strangles means grips around, enclosing
almost drops the last letter

parts.note: a stock is a formal cravat or neckband
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A philosopher is nearly throttled by his own neckwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stoic was a follower of Zeno's school of philosophy.

clue.text: Take credit, limiting doctor's pomposity

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing, so the doctor sits within

parts.note: to boast is to take credit for oneself
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Boasting about a doctor's role reveals his self-importance.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombast is pompous, inflated language, so pomposity of speech.

clue.text: European's warm emotion three quarters occluded

definitions.note: European is: the 's links definition to wordplay

indicators.note: occluded means blocked off, so the emotion is shut in by the quarters

parts.note: three of the four compass points, quarters: south, north and east
love is a warm emotion

explanation.surface: A European's affection is mostly hidden from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three quarters' looks like a fraction, but it means three of the compass points, S, N and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A Slovene is a person from Slovenia, a European country.

clue.text: They leave the country from old seaside towns

parts.note: ex means former
ports are towns on the coast

explanation.surface: People quit the country from former coastal resorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Exports are goods sent out of the country for sale abroad.

clue.text: Judge an aristocrat by his voice

indicators.note: by his voice says the words are heard spoken

parts.note: a count is a nobleman

explanation.surface: You can tell a nobleman by the way he speaks.
explanation.definitionFit: To account something as true is to consider or deem it so, which is to judge it.
